title: The transcranial pulse stimulation (TPS®) as a method in the treatment of the central nervous system of patients with Alzheimer`s dementia
summary: Transcranial pulse stimulation is a therapy used to treat Alzheimer's dementia (AD). TPS® has also been approved for the treatment of AD in Germany. The treatment is intended to improve blood flow to the brain, form new blood vessels and regenerate the nerves. The aim of the treatment is to maintain and promote patients' cognitive abilities for as long as possible. The study will assess and evaluate the development of cognitive performance and the burden of depressive symptoms in patients with AD during treatment with TPS.

interventions.name: Patients with dementia in Alzheimer's disease who are treated with the transcranial pulse stimulation (TPS) in an outpatient setting of a psychiatric-psychosomatic clinic (Wahrendorff Klinikum).

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Main Diagnosis: Alzheimer's Disease
Exclusion criteria:
